resale_co.name: Resale Certificate (Existing Structure Inspection); Transfer Certificate if the home cannot pass
resale_co.valid_for: Resale Certificate: 1 year from issuance. Transfer Certificate: 180 days.
requirements: All construction (UCC) permits closed and all property maintenance violations resolved before the inspection is scheduled
Chimney certification from a licensed chimney sweep or HVAC contractor
Heating system certification from a licensed HVAC contractor or plumber
Yard kept up, with no overgrown grass or weeds and no debris or trash
Reflective house numbers at least 2 inches tall on the front of the house
Secure handrails on every staircase of 4 or more steps
Plumbing working with water flowing from each faucet; electricity, gas and water on
Outlets working, with GFI outlets in bathrooms, kitchen and outdoors
Smoke detectors in all bedrooms and in the hall outside the bedrooms, plus at least one smoke detector and one CO detector on each level
2A-10BC fire extinguisher mounted within 10 feet of the kitchen (Borough ordinance and August 2024 checklist)
Interior and exterior doors open and close properly, exterior doors lock, windows lock and stay open when raised

fees.label: Resale Certificate inspection
fees.quote: Upon making application for a Resale Certificate the property owner shall pay the inspection fee of $100.00, prior to the scheduling of an inspection.

fees.label: Re-inspection after a failed inspection (request within 30 days)
fees.quote: If the subject property fails inspection, the property owner may request a reinspection within thirty (30) days upon payment of a $50.00 reinspection fee.

fees.label: Transfer Certificate application (home that cannot pass the resale inspection)
fees.quote: An application for a Transfer Certificate shall be made on a form prescribed by the Borough and the application fee shall be $100.00.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Existing Structure Inspection Application (check Resale Certificate, or Transfer Certificate if the home will not pass) and pay the $100 fee by cash or check to the Borough Office of Code Enforcement, PO Box 797, Island Heights (office at 1 East End Avenue). Close all permits, resolve violations and hand in the chimney and heating certifications before the inspection is scheduled. For a Transfer Certificate, include a letter from the buyer acknowledging the home may not be occupied until the new owner gets a Resale Certificate or a UCC Certificate of Occupancy.

resale_co.notes: Ordinance 2024-06 (repealing and replacing Borough Code 12-1.3 and adding 12-1.4 Resale Certificate and 12-1.5 Transfer Certificate) is printed in the July 16, 2024 Council minutes, which the Borough posted as a newsletter; the minutes show the final reading and motion to adopt. A Transfer Certificate ($100.00) lets a home that cannot pass be sold, but the new owner must then get a Resale Certificate or UCC Certificate of Occupancy within 180 days and may not occupy it until then. An older Certificate of Occupancy application (December 2023 upload) listed a $35.00 re-inspection fee; the current August 2024 form and the ordinance say $50.00. The Code Enforcement page gives Sean Asay as Code Enforcement Officer (Monday evenings 6 to 8 pm) and Gary Stocco as Zoning Officer, both at 732-270-6415; the email is the Office of Code Enforcement address printed on the form. The Borough also runs a separate Rental Certificate for rentals (valid 2 years or until tenants change). No lead time is published.

requirements: Borough resale inspection (Ordinance 2024-06, August 2024 checklist) still lists a 2A-10BC fire extinguisher within 10 feet of the kitchen, although state law dropped the extinguisher on February 3, 2025

authorities.name: Island Heights Borough Fire Official (municipal fire code enforcing agency)
authorities.how_to_apply: The Borough does not post a smoke and CO certificate application or fee. The Fire Official's office hours are by appointment; call the Borough office at 732-270-6415 or write to the Fire Official at PO Box 797, Island Heights, NJ 08732. The Borough's Resale Certificate inspection also checks smoke and CO detectors; ask whether it serves as the state certificate.

fire_cert.notes: Island Heights Borough is its own fire code enforcing agency (registry code M). The state directory lists it under directory code 1510 (Watchdog code 1511), LEA name 'Island Heights Boro Fire Prev', Fire Official William Richert, phone (732) 270-0388, with the Smoke Detector Compliance line printed as (908) 270-0388 (the area code looks like a typo). The directory's email for him is a personal Gmail address, so it is not used here; the Borough page gives the office phone 732-270-6415 and no email. The Borough's Fire Official page describes commercial inspections only and does not mention resale smoke certificates, so who issues the certificate for a home sale and at what fee is not published.

other_items.label: Open permits and violations
other_items.detail: All UCC permits must be closed and all property maintenance violations resolved before the resale inspection is scheduled.

other_items.label: Chimney and heating certifications
other_items.detail: Chimney certification (licensed chimney sweep or HVAC contractor) and heating system certification (licensed HVAC contractor or plumber) are due before the inspection.
